subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a cron-specific tool policy such as tools.cron.tools.allow/deny, make cron inherit tools.subagents.tools, or keep only per-job toolsAllow plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This defines a scheduled-run tool-execution boundary and a new public config surface, so automation should not choose the permanent precedence or compatibility behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add cron-specific policy
options.body: Introduce tools.cron.tools.allow/deny with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job toolsAllow, then document and test fresh-install and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as covered by tools.subagents.tools, reducing config surface but coupling cron and subagent semantics.

options.title: Keep current safeguards only
options.body: Leave cron control to per-job toolsAllow and duplicate-delivery guards, preserving a smaller config surface while not solving the operator-wide deny request.

recommendation.title: Add cron-specific policy
recommendation.body: Introduce tools.cron.tools.allow/deny with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job toolsAllow, then document and test fresh-install and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across scoped capability profiles, cron behavior, config-sensitive security review, and the prior issue review.
